svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: CareLoop architecture: three trust zones, one policy engine, an independent read-back
svg.desc: An inbound email and its PDF attachments enter as UNTRUSTED data, together with the output of the two LLM agents. Seven deterministic graph nodes, all TRUSTED application code, drive the case. One policy engine reading one rules.yaml decides at three points: the gate node, the Strands BeforeToolCall hook, and the gated tool wrapper. Validated facts live in the CONTROLLED zone. The booking leaves over HTTP to Demo World, a separate process, and verification reads that service back on a separate request.
svg.text: CareLoop
trust zones, the authority gate, and the independent read-back
The model proposes. Deterministic code authorises. A separate read of an external system confirms what happened.

g.text: one of exactly two model calls, and neither holds authority

svg.text: UNTRUSTED
what the world sends, and what the models say

g.text: as data, never as a rule

svg.text: A model's output lands in the same
zone as an attacker's document:
typed, read, and gated like any
other input.
TRUSTED
denied: replan, told a ReasonCode and nothing else
GraphBuilder · every node subclasses MultiAgentBase · bounds from set_max_node_executions, set_execution_timeout, set_node_timeout
Caregiver
approve or reject.
The only other source
of TRUSTED there is.
PolicyEngine
one engine, one rules.yaml, three call sites
ALLOW · DENY · REQUIRE_HUMAN, deterministic, deny by default
rules are declarative in rules.yaml, never encoded in Python
argument classes belong to the tool registry: DESTINATION, AUTHORITY, VALUE
what the model is told back: a closed ReasonCode, never interpolated
BeforeToolCallEvent.cancel_tool
@gated_tool wrapper (backstop)
Two independent points at the tool boundary. Each is
proven sufficient alone; with neither, the attack lands.
Application code, the policy engine and rules.yaml. TRUSTED is never manufactured by validation: it comes from configuration a person wrote, or a person pressing approve.
Case is frozen and transition() is its only writer, so DONE is reachable only from VERIFYING. No graph edge leaves DONE; only an inbound event can.
OUTSIDE CARELOOP
demoworld/ — its own process, its own port. It may
never import careloop, which is what makes reading
it back evidence rather than the agent consulting itself.
GET /clinic/slots
the read-back: a separate request, compared against what
policy authorised — never the booking's own response
POST /clinic/appointments
the one real external effect, carrying the idempotency key
derived from (case_id, action, canonical args)
The other three effects — send_email, upload_document,
grant_portal_access — are simulated, and verification of
those closes the loop on the decision, not on the world.
CONTROLLED
what validation has earned the right to promote, and nothing more

g.text: Promoted UNTRUSTED to CONTROLLED by validation, and
only VALUE-class arguments are promotable at all.
DESTINATION and AUTHORITY never are, whatever a
Frozen. State, evidence, approvals, actions, and an
append-only timeline of what was proposed, what was
allowed or denied, which rule matched, and what
SQLite here, a DynamoDB-shaped interface. The durable
source of truth. Strands session persistence holds
execution context only and is never asked a business

svg.text: validated facts, with provenance
resolved trust is what the engine reads
DEPLOYED
everything above runs in one process on one host; the clinic runs in another

Zone colours are claims about authority, not about code quality: UNTRUSTED means nothing here may decide anything, whoever wrote it.
